figures.name: 5_1_training/train_losses
figures.caption: Training losses for both 80-epoch runs. Raw recorded epochs, without smoothing or interpolation. Losses are native training-framework values.

figures.name: 5_1_training/val_losses
figures.caption: Validation losses for both 80-epoch runs. Raw recorded epochs, without smoothing or interpolation. Losses are native training-framework values.

figures.name: 5_1_training/native_validation_metrics
figures.caption: Native training-time validation metrics. Markers identify selected epochs 22 and 26 on mAP50–95. Native precision/recall use framework reporting, not the final fixed .25 operating point; these are not the final common original-coordinate metrics.

figures.name: 5_2_overall/test_map50_95
figures.caption: Final test eight-class mAP50–95. A–C use standard training; D–F use rarity-only training. In each group the inference order is Standard, SAHI Context, V3. C is the predefined primary pipeline. Bars begin at zero; tiny V3 differences should not be read as established superiority.

figures.name: 5_2_overall/validation_test_map50_95
figures.caption: Comparable validation (3,088 images/914 patients) and test (3,178 images/913 patients) results under the same final deterministic evaluator. C/F use V3 in both partitions. Separate cohorts; this is not a paired validation-minus-test inference.

figures.name: 5_3_classes/class_ap50_95_heatmap
figures.caption: Test AP50–95 for all eight classes; displayed cell labels are rounded to one decimal percent. A–C: standard training; D–F: rarity-only. The full 0–100% scale is shared. Table 3 gives support, including bone lesion (5 objects/4 patients) and bone anomaly (35/14).

figures.name: 5_3_classes/fracture_ap
figures.caption: Fracture AP under the six final conditions. Every panel begins at zero. V3 preserves all three fracture point metrics relative to its corresponding standard inference; rarity-only training does not improve every target. Paired uncertainty is reported separately.

figures.name: 5_3_classes/rarity_class_differences
figures.caption: Rarity-only minus standard training with standard inference (D−A), by class. Points and nominal patient-paired percentile 95% intervals use 500 draws/seed314159; valid counts vary with class presence. All bounds are retained. The sparse-class intervals limit interpretation; this compares two fixed training runs, not a general sampler effect.

figures.name: 5_4_errors/false_positives
figures.caption: Annotation-relative unmatched predictions at confidence .25 and IoU .50 on the test set. These are not clinically confirmed false diagnoses. All six final conditions use the same operating-point matcher.

figures.name: 5_4_errors/recovery_fp_tradeoff
figures.caption: Recovered/lost annotated objects and added unmatched predictions relative to the corresponding standard inference. The panels have separate count scales. Recovery is determined by annotation correspondence, not by the number of changed confidence scores.

figures.name: 5_5_efficiency/latency_and_calls
figures.caption: Measured complete-path mean/p95 latency and actual mean physical calls per image. Three synthetic warmups, loading, export and offline metrics are excluded. Separate sessions and fixed A–F order limit speed comparisons. V3 paired global-prefix ratios are 1.274×/1.243×; p95 is a latency percentile, not a confidence interval.

figures.name: 5_6_uncertainty/main_paired_differences
figures.caption: Main predefined test contrasts: nominal patient-paired percentile 95% intervals from 500 draws/seed314159 (492 valid eight-class replicates). The common scale and zero line retain SAHI/training effects without magnifying tiny V3 changes. C−A is primary; its interval includes zero. Secondary intervals are unadjusted and do not establish clinical validation. Table 4 contains all eleven contrasts.

tables.name: table_1_training_checkpoints
tables.caption: Training and selected checkpoints. Native metrics are the logged values at epochs selected by native eight-class validation mAP50–95; they are distinct from the final evaluator. Steady accumulation excludes the native warmup ramp. Full checkpoint identities are in the source manifest.

tables.name: table_2_final_test_performance
tables.caption: Final test performance at confidence .25 / IoU .50 for operating counts. A/B/C: standard training; D/E/F: rarity-only. Inference order within each group: Standard, SAHI Context, CG-ALR V3. C is primary. AP uses the common final deterministic evaluator. Displayed values are rounded; exact values remain in the verified Phase 5D results.json. The source manifest records displayed cells and source hashes.

tables.name: table_3_class_AP_support
tables.caption: Test class-specific AP50–95 and support. AP columns are percentages rounded to two decimals; tiny V3 changes can disappear at this precision. All 7,361 annotations are included. Bone-lesion and bone-anomaly support is sparse. AP50/AP75 remain available in the verified Phase 5D AP.csv.

tables.name: table_4_paired_comparisons
tables.caption: All eleven predefined paired test comparisons. Patient bootstrap: 500 draws, seed 314159. Eight-class AP is undefined in samples missing a class; 492 samples contribute here. Secondary intervals are unadjusted for multiplicity. These are not clinical-validation or general training-seed uncertainty intervals.
